chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibrahim ibn Uthman ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said: 'There is a man who has a debt owed to me, and his house is pledged as collateral (rahn). I wish to sell it.' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'I advise you by Allah not to evict him from the shadow of his head (i.e., do not evict him while the debt remains unpaid).'

key_terms.أُعِيذُكَ: I seek refuge for you / I advise you strongly
key_terms.رَهْناً: Collateral or pledge (a property held as security for a debt)
key_terms.ظِلِّ رَأْسِهِ: Shadow of his head (idiom for remaining in one's place/home)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on evicting a debtor from their home if it is used as collateral for a debt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a creditor not to evict a debtor from their home while the debt remains unpaid, using the phrase 'from the shadow of his head' to signify the debtor's right to shelter. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-ghurm bi al-ghurm* (liability accompanies ownership/use), prioritizing the debtor's basic housing needs over immediate liquidation of the collateral. It underscores the ethical dimension of debt collection, encouraging leniency and protection of the debtor's dignity during the repayment period.
